name: Drop Deployment
description: Owns the first sixty seconds of a match: selecting a point on the drop path, the skydive down, and the landing. Selection happens on the map because 'where do I commit' is the genre's opening bet — hot-drop for loot density, cold-drop for safety — and the component keeps the commitment binding once made, since a re-pickable drop deletes the bet. The descent is a scripted movement state with capped steering: fully free flight would turn deployment into a traversal exploit that skips the ground game. The moment boots touch ground, control returns to the normal movement stack and touchdown is movement.ground_sensor's event like any other landing; this component's responsibility ends exactly there.

inputs.name: dropPathDurationSeconds
inputs.description: How long the drop vehicle takes to cross the map. Players may exit at any point along it; the path is published on the map so the decision is informed, not a dice roll.

inputs.name: steerSpeed
inputs.description: Horizontal steering speed while descending. Capped well below ground sprint speed so the dive closes distance vertically but cannot be used as a lateral travel tool.

inputs.name: diveSpeed
inputs.description: Maximum vertical descent rate. Racing the drop is real strategy — first to the loot wins it — so dive speed is a tunable, not a constant.

inputs.name: minDeployHeight
inputs.description: Altitude at which the final descent stage (chute, glide, whatever the fiction says) forces open. Exists so a player cannot free-fall to ground level and skip the vulnerable slow-descent window.

outputs.name: isDropping
outputs.description: True from drop-vehicle exit until landing. Combat and loot systems gate on this — a dropping player is a spectator with velocity.

outputs.name: selectedDropPoint
outputs.description: The committed landing target, set once at selection and never revised. Downstream systems (squad pings, AI drop logic) read this rather than re-deriving intent.
